definitions.explanation: A person making the pilgrimage to the 88 temples associated with the Buddhist monk Kūkai (Kōbō Daishi) on the island of Shikoku.
The act of visiting the 88 temples of Shikoku, either on foot, by bus, or by car. The full walking route is approximately 1,200 km.

examples.japanese: お{遍路|へんろ}さんが{歩|ある}いている。
{白|しろ}い{衣装|いしょう}を{着|き}たお{遍路|へんろ}さんを{見|み}かけた。
examples.english: I spotted a pilgrim wearing white clothing.

examples.japanese: {退職後|たいしょくご}にお{遍路|へんろ}に{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: After retiring, I set out on the pilgrimage.

examples.japanese: {四国|しこく}のお{遍路|へんろ}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{歩|ある}くと{約|やく}{四十日|よんじゅうにち}かかる。
examples.english: Walking the entire Shikoku pilgrimage takes about forty days.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{毎年|まいとし}{少|すこ}しずつお{遍路|へんろ}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: My mother continues the pilgrimage little by little each year.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{外国人|がいこくじん}のお{遍路|へんろ}さんも{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Recently, the number of foreign pilgrims has been increasing.

notes: The お prefix is honorific; the base form is {遍路|へんろ}. Pilgrims are respectfully called お{遍路|へんろ}さん. The traditional pilgrim wears a {白衣|びゃくえ} (white robe) and carries a {金剛杖|こんごうづえ} (walking staff). Along the route, locals often offer {接待|せったい} (hospitality) such as food, drink, or a place to rest. The pilgrimage can be completed all at once ({通|とお}し{打|う}ち) or in sections over multiple trips ({区切|くぎ}り{打|う}ち). Also called {四国八十八箇所|しこくはちじゅうはっかしょ} (Shikoku 88 Sacred Places).
